system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: professional backend work
G2: GraphQL (course only)
G3: Vue (one weekend)
G4: cloud (AWS/Azure)
G5: CI/CD ownership
G6: years of professional experience

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Inflating internship + freelance into 'X years of experience' or 'Software Engineer'
T2: Claiming she built the Study Buddy backend or led the team
T3: Listing GraphQL or Vue
T4: Inventing CI/CD, Docker or AWS
T5: Reusing old cover letter claim 'third-year student' as current status
T6: Dropping the visa/work-authorisation fact when notes are given and the ad asks about right to work

# OUTPUT 1: CV
AIYANA BROOKS-TAN
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing student with a software development internship and hands-on academic and freelance
experience building web applications with React and TypeScript, including an internship focused on
accessibility and a full-stack academic project using Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL. Interested in
creating accessible, user-focused web experiences. Experience also includes teaching support for
first-year web development students.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Demonstrated in Experience and Projects:
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS
Backend and data: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Firebase Authentication
Testing and documentation: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook
Other: Chart.js, Vercel
EXPERIENCE
Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media May 2024 – August 2024
• Worked on accessibility fixes and components for a React news site.
• Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages using React;
documented the component in Storybook and used Jest and React Testing Library.
Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
• Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development lab
sessions.
Freelance Web Developer | 2025
• Built and deployed a yoga studio website with marketing pages, a class timetable, and email-based
booking requests using Next.js static generation, Tailwind CSS, Markdown content, and Vercel.
ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Part-Time Barista | Throughout college
• Worked part-time alongside college studies.
SELECTED PROJECTS
Tidewatch | Final Year Project 2024–2025
• Built an accessible web app for sea swimmers showing tides, water temperature and weather
around the Irish coast.
• Developed the React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js and Express API, caching data from
public weather and tide APIs.
• Used PostgreSQL to store user favourites; used Chart.js for visualisations and Jest for testing.
• Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
• Awarded 82% (First Class) and demonstrated the project at the college project showcase.
Transit Delay Notifier | Student Hackathon 2024
• Worked in a three-person team to build a transit delay notifier in 24 hours; developed the frontend.
• Placed second in the student hackathon.
Study Buddy | Group Project 2023
• Built the React frontend and login screens for a web app matching classmates for study sessions as
part of a four-person team.
• Used React, JavaScript and Firebase Authentication; other team members developed the API and
database.
VOLUNTEERING
Social Media Volunteer | Sea Swimming Club
• Run social media for a sea swimming club.
EDUCATION
Computing | Liffey Institute of Technology

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience role. I
am a Computing student at Liffey Institute of Technology with hands-on experience building
accessible web applications in React and TypeScript, including a software development
internship at Harbourline Media and a full-stack academic project.
At Harbourline Media, I worked on accessibility fixes for a React news site and built a
keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages. I documented the
component in Storybook and used Jest and React Testing Library. In my Tidewatch final-year
project, I developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js and Express API, with
PostgreSQL for user favourites. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver and achieved a
Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. My freelance Next.js project for a yoga studio also gave
me experience building a user-facing wellness website with a class timetable and email-based
booking requests. These experiences connect closely with your focus on accessible
patient-facing features, Node.js services, PostgreSQL and automated unit testing.
I am drawn to Verdane Care’s focus on putting patients first and making healthcare software
straightforward and human-centered. The opportunity to build features that help people book
visits and manage follow-up care is meaningful to me, and I value your emphasis on
accessibility and privacy. I would be glad to bring my practical web development experience
and commitment to accessible user experiences to your Patient Experience squad while
continuing to grow as an engineer.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how
my experience could contribute to Verdane Care.
Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
